title: Police blameless in cocaine overdose death
article: He died covered in vomit, lying next to a police cruiser while an officer pleaded with his friend to tell him what he swallowed.

An inquest report into the March 2007 death of Randy George Krasnesky released Wednesday said the 35-year-old died of a massive overdose after he swallowed a condom full of cocaine. The report concludes paramedics and officers could have done nothing differently to save Krasnesky's life.
Mounties had pulled over Krasnesky and his friend, a University of Winnipeg student, in Selkirk one night after receiving a tip the young woman was possibly dealing drugs.
After officers pulled their van over, officers found marijuana on Krasnesky and put him in a nearby cruiser.
From there, Krasnesky quickly turned from "co-operative, laughing and in good spirits" to "loud, abrupt, and angry," swearing at police.

Mounties testified at the inquest they asked his companion what he'd swallowed, but she said repeatedly she had no idea. Krasnesky, who was shaking violently and convulsing, died about an hour later at hospital.
Provincial chief medical examiner Dr. Thambirajah Balachandra said a subsequent autopsy turned up a deadly dose of cocaine in Krasnesky's body.

"Following a detailed review of the evidence and the circumstances relating to Krasnesky's death there is nothing, in my view, that can be recommended to prevent similar deaths from occurring in the future," provincial court associate chief Judge Michel Chartier said in his inquest report.
